law_changes.rebate_87a_limit: Raised to Rs. 12,00,000 (tax liability Nil up to 12L taxable income)

Hand-coded rules.what_broke: 18 regression tests expecting FY 2024-25 slab taxes failed immediately during pytest run.
Hand-coded rules.silent_failures_details: None. Type checks, assertion errors, and regression tests made all discrepancies loud and explicit.

LLM at query time.what_broke: Zero code broke. Syntax and API calls succeeded with HTTP 200.
LLM at query time.silent_failures_details: CRITICAL: Silent semantic hallucinations. In marginal relief zone (gross 12.8L), the LLM calculated normal slab tax (Rs. 60,750 + cess) instead of applying Section 87A proviso cap (Rs. 5,000 + cess = Rs. 5,200). On 10L income, it occasionally hallucinated the old 7L rebate limit from pre-trained weights despite the prompt text. The API threw zero errors, returning incorrect tax figures silently to the user.
LLM at query time.audit_safety: DANGEROUS. Silent calculation errors in production without observability.

LLM-compiled rules.what_broke: Compilation generated compiled_fy25_26.py; initial compilation missed marginal relief cap on 12L until prompt refinement.
LLM-compiled rules.silent_failures_details: None in production. Because compilation occurs offline before deployment, the compiler output was audited against the test suite, the marginal relief formula was verified once, and deployed with zero runtime drift.
LLM-compiled rules.audit_safety: VERY HIGH. Offline LLM compilation paired with deterministic CI/CD verification.
